skills.title: Read and write numbers up to crores with Indian commas
Convert between Indian (lakh, crore) and international (million, billion) names
Compare and order large numbers using place value

expectations: After thousands come lakhs (1,00,000) and crores (1,00,00,000) in the Indian system
1 lakh = 100 thousand, 1 crore = 100 lakh = 10 million, and 10 lakh = 1 million
Indian commas: the first after 3 digits from the right, then after every 2 digits; international commas: after every 3 digits
Only the grouping changes between the two systems; the number itself stays the same
A number with more digits is bigger; with the same number of digits, compare from the leftmost place

signs: Converts 5 crore to 5 million
Says a 'millionaire' has a crore rupees
Counts 6 zeros for a crore

Lakhs come just before ten thousands.
4 lakh is 4,00,000; add 25 thousand to get 4,___,000.

items.prompt_en: A cricket app says 1.2 million people watched a match online. How many lakh is that?
items.prompt_hi: Ek cricket app kehta hai 1.2 million logon ne match online dekha. Yeh kitne lakh hue?
items.answer: 12 lakh
hints: How many lakh make one million?

items.prompt_en: Guess first: is 1 crore more than, less than, or equal to 1 million? Then check by counting zeros.
items.prompt_hi: Pehle andaaza lagao: 1 crore, 1 million se zyada hai, kam hai ya barabar? Phir zero gin ke check karo.
items.answer: More: 1 crore has 7 zeros and 1 million has 6, so 1 crore = 10 million

items.prompt_en: Look at 98,76,543 and 1,02,34,567. The first starts with bigger digits. Which number is greater, and what decides it?
items.prompt_hi: 98,76,543 aur 1,02,34,567 dekho. Pehla bade digits se shuru hota hai. Kaun bada hai, aur kya decide karta hai?
items.answer: 1,02,34,567 is greater: it has 8 digits (more than a crore) while 98,76,543 has only 7
hints: What do you check before looking at the first digit?

items.prompt_en: Ten lakh is written 10,00,000 and one million is written 1,000,000. Are these different numbers? Why do the commas look different?
items.prompt_hi: Das lakh ko 10,00,000 likhte hain aur ek million ko 1,000,000. Kya yeh alag numbers hain? Commas alag kyun dikhte hain?
items.answer: Same number; only the grouping differs: Indian groups the first 3 digits then pairs (lakh, crore), international groups in threes (thousand, million)
hints: Indian groups in 3 then ___; international always in 3.

items.prompt_en: Riya wrote 'thirty lakh four thousand' as 3,04,000. Find her mistake and fix it.
items.prompt_hi: Riya ne 'tees lakh chaar hazaar' ko 3,04,000 likha. Galti dhoondo aur theek karo.
items.answer: She wrote 3 lakh 4 thousand; thirty lakh is 30,00,000, so the number is 30,04,000
hints: What does 3,04,000 say when you read it?

items.prompt_en: A state budget headline says ₹2,500 crore. Write it in numerals with Indian commas, then say how many billion rupees it is.
items.prompt_hi: Ek state budget ki headline mein ₹2,500 crore likha hai. Isse Indian commas ke saath numerals mein likho, phir batao kitne billion rupaye hue.
items.answer: ₹25,00,00,00,000, which is 25 billion
hints: How many zeros does 1 crore have?

items.prompt_en: Your state has 7 crore 25 lakh people. A country abroad has 70 million. Which has more people?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare state mein 7 crore 25 lakh log hain. Ek videsh ke desh mein 70 million. Kahan zyada log hain?
items.answer: Your state: 7 crore 25 lakh = 72.5 million, which is more than 70 million

items.prompt_en: Put the digits of 5,06,08,020 into a place-value chart. What is the 6 worth?
items.prompt_hi: 5,06,08,020 ke digits place-value chart mein rakho. 6 ki value kitni hai?

items.prompt_hi: Tumhare cousin ko lagta hai 1 crore aur 1 million same hain. Use zero ya place-value chart se check karna sikhao.
items.answer: 1 crore is 1 followed by 7 zeros, 1 million is 1 followed by 6 zeros, so 1 crore = 10 million; also 10 lakh = 1 million
hints: Write both numbers with all their zeros.
7 zeros and ___ zeros: one extra place.

items.prompt_en: Quick, from memory: which is bigger, 50 lakh or 5 million, or are they equal?

items.answer: They are equal (5 million = 50 lakh)
hints: How many lakh make a million?

skills.title: Decide whether a situation needs an exact or an approximate value
Round large numbers to a sensible place (thousand, lakh, crore)
Judge how big the error from rounding is

expectations: Some situations need exact values (fees, bank balances, exam marks), others only need the size (crowds, distances, populations)
To round, look only at the digit just right of the rounding place: 5 or more rounds up, less than 5 keeps it
A rounded number is not wrong: it is a close, simpler value chosen on purpose
The rounding place depends on the purpose and on how big the number is
The rounding error is the gap between the exact and rounded values, and it should be small compared with the number

misconceptions.belief: Believes rounded figures in news are 'wrong' or lies
signs: Says the newspaper lied because the count is not exact
Insists on exact counts even for crowds
Distrusts 'about' and 'nearly'

diagnostic.prompt_en: A news report says 'about 2 crore people visited the mela'. The exact count was 1,98,43,210. Was the report wrong?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Khabar mein likha 'mele mein lagbhag 2 crore log aaye'. Asli ginti 1,98,43,210 thi. Kya report galat thi?

options.text: No, it rounded to a sensible value
Yes, because the number is not exact
Yes, it should have said 1 crore

hints: Which two lakhs is it between?

items.prompt_en: Which of these needs an exact number: (a) distance from Delhi to Agra for a trip plan, (b) the school fee you transfer online, (c) the crowd at a cricket match?
items.prompt_hi: Inmein se kisme exact number chahiye: (a) trip ke liye Delhi se Agra ki doori, (b) online bhari jaane wali school fee, (c) cricket match ki bheed?
items.answer: (b) the school fee
hints: Where would a small mistake cause a problem?
Money paid must match to the rupee.
Distance and crowds only need the ___.

items.prompt_en: Predict before rounding: when 7,49,999 is rounded to the nearest lakh, will it go up to 8 lakh or stay at 7 lakh? Then check.
items.prompt_hi: Round karne se pehle andaaza lagao: 7,49,999 ko lakh tak round karein toh 8 lakh banega ya 7 lakh rahega? Phir check karo.
items.answer: It stays at 7,00,000, because 49,999 is less than 50,000
hints: What is halfway between 7 lakh and 8 lakh?

items.prompt_en: Two reporters round 1,96,48,000 people. One writes 'about 2 crore', the other 'about 1 crore 96 lakh'. Both are right. What is different?

items.answer: They rounded to different places: nearest crore versus nearest lakh; the second is closer, the first is simpler
hints: Which place did each reporter round to?
One rounded to crores, the other to lakhs.

items.prompt_en: Why is it fine for a newspaper to write 'about 3 lakh people' at a rally, but not fine for a bank passbook to show 'about ₹3 lakh'?
items.prompt_hi: Akhbaar mein 'lagbhag 3 lakh log' likhna theek kyun hai, par bank passbook mein 'lagbhag ₹3 lakh' likhna theek kyun nahi?
items.answer: A crowd cannot be counted exactly and readers only need its size; money in an account is counted to the rupee and must be exact
hints: Can anyone count a rally crowd exactly?
Think about who needs each number and why.
A bank balance must match to the ___.
Crowd: size is enough; money: must be exact.

items.prompt_en: Aman rounded 3,45,000 to the nearest lakh like this: 3,45,000 → 3,50,000 → 4,00,000. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Aman ne 3,45,000 ko lakh tak aise round kiya: 3,45,000 → 3,50,000 → 4,00,000. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. Round in one step using the ten-thousands digit: 4 is less than 5, so 3,45,000 rounds to 3,00,000
hints: Which digit should he look at for lakhs?
That digit is 4, which is ___ than 5.

items.prompt_en: A film earned ₹2,87,46,00,000. Round it to the nearest crore.
items.prompt_hi: Ek film ne ₹2,87,46,00,000 kamaaye. Ise sabse paas ke crore tak round karo.
hints: How many crore is it, roughly?
It is 287 crore and some lakh.

items.prompt_en: A shopkeeper rounds each bill to the nearest ₹100 before adding: ₹249, ₹349, ₹449 and ₹149. How far is his rounded total from the exact total?
items.prompt_hi: Ek dukaandaar har bill ko jodne se pehle sabse paas ke ₹100 tak round karta hai: ₹249, ₹349, ₹449 aur ₹149. Uska rounded total asli total se kitna door hai?
items.answer: ₹196 short: rounded total ₹1,000, exact total ₹1,196
hints: Every bill ends in 49, so each rounds down.

items.prompt_en: Mark 6,30,000 on a number line from 6,00,000 to 7,00,000. Which lakh is it nearer to?
items.prompt_hi: 6,00,000 se 7,00,000 tak ki number line par 6,30,000 mark karo. Yeh kis lakh ke zyada paas hai?
items.answer: 6,00,000: it is 30,000 away from 6 lakh and 70,000 away from 7 lakh

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend how to round 8,51,200 to the nearest lakh, and why the rounded value is still 'correct' even though it is not exact.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki 8,51,200 ko lakh tak kaise round karte hain, aur rounded value exact na hote hue bhi 'sahi' kyun hai.
items.answer: Look at the ten-thousands digit, 5: 5 or more rounds up, so 9,00,000. It is a close value chosen on purpose; the error is only 48,800
hints: The digit just right of the lakh place.

items.prompt_en: From memory: when you round to the nearest thousand, which digit do you look at?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: hazaar tak round karte waqt kaunsa digit dekhte hain?
items.answer: The hundreds digit (just right of the thousands place)
hints: Which place is just right of thousands?
Places go thousands, hundreds, tens, ones.

items.prompt_en: The train route from Mumbai to Kolkata is about 1,968 km. Round it to the nearest hundred km.
items.prompt_hi: Mumbai se Kolkata ka train route lagbhag 1,968 km hai. Ise sabse paas ke sau km tak round karo.
hints: The tens digit is 6, so it rounds ___.

skills.title: Multiply numbers ending in zeros by multiplying the non-zero parts and counting zeros
Estimate products of large numbers by rounding first
Use powers of 10 to judge the size and number of digits of a product

expectations: Split off the zeros, multiply the non-zero parts, then attach all the zeros from both numbers: 3,000 × 400 = 12 followed by 5 zeros = 12,00,000
If the non-zero parts multiply to a number ending in 0 (5 × 4 = 20), that zero is extra and must be kept
Multiplying by 10 shifts every digit one place left
Rounding each number before multiplying gives a quick estimate
An estimate tells roughly how many digits the exact answer should have

misconceptions.belief: Miscounts zeros when multiplying numbers like 3,000 × 400
signs: Attaches zeros from only one number
Answers off by a factor of 10

diagnostic.prompt_hi: 3,000 × 400 kitna hai?

signs: Counts the zero in 30 as one of the attached zeros

items.prompt_hi: Bina guna kiye andaaza lagao: 25 × 4,000 mein kitne digit honge? Phir check karo.

items.prompt_en: Compare 40 × 50, 4 × 500 and 400 × 5. What do you notice, and why does it happen?
items.prompt_hi: 40 × 50, 4 × 500 aur 400 × 5 ko compare karo. Kya dikhta hai, aur aisa kyun hota hai?
items.answer: All three equal 2,000: each is 4 × 5 = 20 with two more zeros; moving a zero from one number to the other does not change the product
hints: Count the zeros in each pair.
Each pair has 2 zeros in total.

items.prompt_en: Why does multiplying a whole number by 1,000 put exactly three zeros at its end?
items.prompt_hi: Kisi whole number ko 1,000 se guna karne par end mein theek teen zero kyun lagte hain?
items.answer: 1,000 = 10 × 10 × 10; each × 10 shifts every digit one place left and leaves a 0 in the ones place, so three shifts give three zeros
hints: Each × 10 moves every digit one place ___.

items.prompt_en: Kabir wrote 2,500 × 40 = 10,000. Check his work.
items.prompt_hi: Kabir ne likha 2,500 × 40 = 10,000. Uska kaam check karo.
items.answer: Wrong: 25 × 4 = 100, then attach the 3 zeros, so 2,500 × 40 = 1,00,000

items.prompt_en: About how many seconds are there in a year? Round sensibly and multiply.
items.prompt_hi: Ek saal mein lagbhag kitne second hote hain? Samajhdaari se round karke guna karo.
items.answer: About 3 crore seconds (exactly 3,15,36,000 in a 365-day year)
hints: Start with seconds in an hour.
60 × 60 = 3,600 seconds in an hour; × 24 = 86,400 in a day.

items.prompt_en: A stadium has 48 blocks with 1,020 seats in each. Estimate the total number of seats.
items.prompt_hi: Ek stadium mein 48 block hain, har block mein 1,020 seat. Kul seats ka andaaza lagao.

items.prompt_en: Write 7 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 as one number with Indian commas, and say it in words.
items.prompt_hi: 7 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 ko ek number ki tarah Indian commas ke saath likho, aur shabdon mein bolo.
items.answer: 7,00,000, seven lakh

items.prompt_en: Show a friend how a quick estimate tells whether 389 × 51 = 1,98,390 is right.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko dikhao ki ek jaldi ka andaaza kaise batata hai ki 389 × 51 = 1,98,390 sahi hai ya nahi.
items.answer: Estimate 400 × 50 = 20,000, so the product should be near 20,000; 1,98,390 is about ten times too big (the real answer is 19,839)

items.prompt_hi: Jaldi yaad karo: 90 × 9,000 = ?

skills.title: Write an arithmetic expression for a word situation
Compare two expressions by reasoning about their parts, without full calculation
Tell a situation that matches a given expression

expectations: An expression is numbers joined by operations that stands for a value, e.g. 3 × 15 + 2 × 10 for 3 samosas at ₹15 and 2 chai at ₹10
The same value can be written as many different expressions
Expressions can be compared by reasoning: 23 + 48 = 24 + 47, because one part goes up by 1 and the other goes down by 1
Taking away more leaves less: 100 − 37 < 100 − 29
'7 less than 30' starts with 30 and takes away 7: 30 − 7

misconceptions.belief: Thinks an expression must always be fully calculated before it can be compared
signs: Adds both sides of 99 + 47 vs 47 + 100 before answering
Says 'I can't tell until I solve it'
Never looks at how the parts changed

workedExample.problem: Two lines cross. One angle is 72°. Find the other three.

The angle across from that 108° is also 108°.
The four angles are 72°, 108°, 72°, 108°; they add to 360°.

Check a statement against data: true, false or cannot tell

A statement checked against data is true, false, or cannot be decided from this data
Two things rising together does not prove one causes the other
One case or a few cases is not enough to make a claim about everyone
To check a statement, find the exact numbers it talks about and compare them

misconceptions.belief: Believes data always proves a claim
signs: Says 'the table proves it' for any claim
Treats things that happen together as cause and effect
Never asks what else could explain the numbers

diagnostic.prompt_en: In a town, ice-cream sales and the number of hot days both go up in May. Does this prove ice-cream causes hot days?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek shehar mein May mein ice-cream ki bikri aur garam dinon ki ginti dono badhti hain. Kya isse saabit hota hai ki ice-cream se garmi aati hai?

signs: Calls a statement false when the data says nothing about it
Never uses 'cannot tell'
Guesses beyond the table

diagnostic.prompt_en: A table shows the heights of 30 students of class 7. Statement: 'Class 7 students are the tallest in the school.'
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek table mein class 7 ke 30 bachchon ki height hai. Statement: 'Class 7 ke bachche school mein sabse lambe hain.'

remediation.representation: A sorting mat with three trays: true, false, cannot tell
remediation.moveShape: Child points to the numbers in the table that the statement needs; ask whether those numbers are there at all

misconceptions.belief: Makes a general claim from one case or a very small sample
signs: Says 'March is rainier' from one rainy March day
Surveys 5 friends and talks about all of India
Uses one high score to say a player is better

options.text: No: compare the monthly totals, over several years

remediation.moveShape: Child compares the one-day bar with the monthly bars; ask how many days make up the July total

items.prompt_en: Rain (mm) in a city: June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. Which month had the most rain?

items.answer: July (250 mm)

items.prompt_en: Rain (mm) in a city: June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. True or false: August had more than double September's rain.
items.prompt_hi: Ek shehar mein baarish (mm): June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. Sahi ya galat: August mein September se double se zyada baarish hui.
items.answer: False: double of 120 is 240, and August had 230

items.prompt_en: Rain (mm) in a city: June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. What was the total rain from June to September?
items.prompt_hi: Ek shehar mein baarish (mm): June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. June se September tak kul kitni baarish hui?
items.answer: 740 mm

items.prompt_en: Rain (mm) in a city: June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. Compare two statements: (a) 'This year July was rainier than June.' (b) 'July is always rainier than June.' Which can this table check?
items.prompt_hi: Ek shehar mein baarish (mm): June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. Do statements compare karo: (a) 'Is saal July, June se zyada baarish wala tha.' (b) 'July hamesha June se zyada baarish wala hota hai.' Yeh table kaunsa check kar sakti hai?
items.answer: Only (a), which is true (250 > 140); (b) needs data from many years
hints: How many years does the table show?

items.prompt_en: Rain (mm) in a city: June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. Which question can the table answer: (a) Which month had the least rain? (b) Why does it rain so much in July?
items.prompt_hi: Ek shehar mein baarish (mm): June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. Table kaunse sawaal ka jawab de sakti hai: (a) Kis mahine sabse kam baarish hui? (b) July mein itni baarish kyun hoti hai?
items.answer: (a): September, 120 mm; the table has amounts, not reasons
hints: What kind of facts are in the table?
A 'why' needs reasons, which the table does ___ have.

items.prompt_en: Rain (mm) in a city: June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. Why can't this table tell us whether it will rain on 15 July next year?
items.prompt_hi: Ek shehar mein baarish (mm): June 140, July 250, August 230, September 120. Yeh table yeh kyun nahi bata sakti ki agle saal 15 July ko baarish hogi ya nahi?
items.answer: It only has monthly totals for one year; it has no single days and nothing about the future
hints: Does the table show single days?
And is next year in the table? ___.
It has neither single days nor next year.

items.prompt_en: Riya noticed that students who sat in the front row got higher marks in one test. She says: 'Sitting in front makes you score more.' Check her claim.
items.prompt_hi: Riya ne dekha ki ek test mein aage baithne wale bachchon ke marks zyada aaye. Woh kehti hai: 'Aage baithne se marks badhte hain.' Uska claim check karo.
items.answer: Not proven: the data shows the two go together, not that one causes the other; keen students may choose the front, and it was only one test
hints: Maybe keen students pick the front.
Going together is not the same as ___.
Not proven: together does not mean cause.

items.prompt_en: Runs in three matches: Aarav 45, 12, 78; Kabir 30, 55, 60. Aarav says: 'I scored more runs in total, because my 78 is the highest.' Check.
items.prompt_hi: Teen matches ke runs: Aarav 45, 12, 78; Kabir 30, 55, 60. Aarav kehta hai: 'Total runs mere zyada hain, kyunki mera 78 sabse zyada hai.' Check karo.
items.answer: False: Aarav's total is 135 and Kabir's is 145; one high score does not decide the total

items.prompt_en: Turn this claim into a question and say what data you would collect: 'More children in our class walk to school than come by bus.'
items.prompt_hi: Is claim ko ek sawaal mein badlo aur batao kaunsa data ikattha karoge: 'Hamari class mein bus se zyada bachche paidal school aate hain.'
items.answer: Question: How do children in our class come to school? Data: a tally of each child's way (walk, bus, cycle, auto…), then compare walk and bus
acceptable: how do children come to school
hints: So we must ask every child how they ___.
Ask everyone how they come and tally it.

items.prompt_en: You ask 5 friends and 4 of them like mango ice-cream. Predict: can you say 80% of children in India like mango ice-cream?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne 5 doston se poocha aur 4 ko mango ice-cream pasand hai. Andaaza lagao: kya keh sakte ho ki India ke 80% bachchon ko mango ice-cream pasand hai?
items.answer: No: 5 friends are too few and are not like all children in India
hints: How many children did you ask?
To speak about India, you would need ___ more children from many places.
No: the sample is too small.

items.prompt_en: The school canteen wants to know whether to make more idli or more poha. What question would you ask, and what data would you collect?
items.prompt_hi: School canteen jaanna chahti hai ki idli zyada banaye ya poha. Tum kya sawaal poochoge aur kaunsa data ikattha karoge?
items.answer: Ask which is chosen more; record how many plates of each are sold every day for a couple of weeks and compare the totals
hints: What would show which is more popular?
Count each for many ___, not just one.
Record daily sales for two weeks and compare.

items.prompt_en: Teach a friend how to check a statement using a table of data.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao ki data ki table se statement kaise check karte hain.
items.answer: Find the numbers the statement talks about, compare them, then decide true, false, or 'cannot tell from this data' if those numbers are not there
hints: What do you look for first?
If they are missing, the answer is ___.
Compare: true, false or cannot tell.

items.prompt_en: From memory: what three answers can a statement get when you check it against data?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se: data se check karne par statement ke teen kaunse jawab ho sakte hain?
items.answer: True, false, or cannot tell from this data
hints: The third is when the data ___ say.

skills.title: Find the mean (average) of a data set
Find the median, ordering the data first
Find the mode and choose the most suitable representative value

expectations: Mean = total ÷ number of values; it is the equal share if the total were levelled out
The mean need not be one of the data values
Median = middle value after putting the data in order; with an even count, take the mean of the middle two
Mode = the value that occurs most often
One extreme value pulls the mean a lot but hardly moves the median, so the median can be a better 'typical' value

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the mean must be one of the data values
signs: Rejects 8 as the mean of 4, 7, 10, 11
Picks the middle data value as the mean
Rounds the mean to the nearest data value

diagnostic.prompt_en: Runs scored: 4, 7, 10, 11. What is the mean?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Bane runs: 4, 7, 10, 11. Mean kya hai?

options.text: 7 or 10, because the mean must be one of the scores

remediation.representation: Towers of blocks levelled into equal heights
remediation.moveShape: Child moves blocks from tall towers to short ones until all are equal; ask whether any original tower was that height

misconceptions.belief: Ignores how one extreme value distorts the mean
signs: Calls ₹30,000 the typical salary when four of five earn about ₹13,000
Always uses the mean
Does not notice a very large or small value

diagnostic.prompt_en: Five people earn ₹12,000, ₹13,000, ₹14,000, ₹15,000 and ₹96,000. Which is a better 'typical' salary: the mean (₹30,000) or the median (₹14,000)?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Paanch log ₹12,000, ₹13,000, ₹14,000, ₹15,000 aur ₹96,000 kamaate hain. 'Typical' salary ke liye kaunsa behtar hai: mean (₹30,000) ya median (₹14,000)?

options.text: The median, because the ₹96,000 pulls the mean up
The mean, it is always best

remediation.representation: A seesaw balance point that shifts when one heavy weight is placed far out
remediation.moveShape: Child removes the ₹96,000 and recomputes both values; ask which one changed a lot

misconceptions.belief: Takes the middle value without putting the data in order
signs: Says the median of 9, 2, 7, 4, 5 is 7
Points to the middle of the list as written
Skips sorting

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is the median of 9, 2, 7, 4, 5?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 9, 2, 7, 4, 5 ka median kya hai?

remediation.representation: Number cards lined up from smallest to largest, with the middle card lifted
remediation.moveShape: Child sorts the cards first and then finds the middle one; ask whether the middle changes if the cards are shuffled

items.prompt_en: Find the mean of 6, 8 and 10.
items.prompt_hi: 6, 8 aur 10 ka mean nikaalo.

items.prompt_en: A batter scores 32, 45, 18, 60 and 25 runs in five matches. What are the average runs per match?
items.prompt_hi: Ek batter paanch matches mein 32, 45, 18, 60 aur 25 runs banata hai. Har match ka average kitna?
items.answer: 36 runs

items.prompt_en: Find the median of 9, 2, 7, 4, 5.
items.prompt_hi: 9, 2, 7, 4, 5 ka median nikaalo.
hints: What must you do before finding the middle?

items.prompt_en: Find the median of 3, 8, 5, 12.
items.prompt_hi: 3, 8, 5, 12 ka median nikaalo.
items.answer: 6.5: in order 3, 5, 8, 12; the middle two are 5 and 8, and (5 + 8) ÷ 2 = 6.5

items.prompt_en: Shoe sizes in a group: 5, 6, 6, 7, 6, 8, 5. What is the mode?
items.prompt_hi: Ek group ke joote ke size: 5, 6, 6, 7, 6, 8, 5. Mode kya hai?
items.answer: 6 (it occurs 3 times)

items.prompt_en: The mean of 4, 7, 10 and 11 is 8, but 8 is not in the list. Why is that fine?
items.prompt_hi: 4, 7, 10 aur 11 ka mean 8 hai, par 8 list mein nahi hai. Yeh theek kyun hai?
items.answer: The mean is the equal share of the total (32 ÷ 4 = 8); levelling out the values can give a number none of them had
hints: The mean is an equal share, so it need not be a data value.

items.prompt_en: Five people earn ₹12,000, ₹13,000, ₹14,000, ₹15,000 and ₹96,000. Find the mean and the median. Which describes a typical person better?
items.prompt_hi: Paanch log ₹12,000, ₹13,000, ₹14,000, ₹15,000 aur ₹96,000 kamaate hain. Mean aur median nikaalo. Typical insaan ko kaun behtar batata hai?
items.answer: Mean ₹30,000, median ₹14,000; the median is better because the one large salary pulls the mean up
hints: Mean ₹30,000, median ₹14,000: the median is more typical.

items.prompt_en: The mean of 5 numbers is 10. Predict what happens to the mean if a sixth number, 40, is added. Then find it.
items.prompt_hi: 5 numbers ka mean 10 hai. Andaaza lagao, chhatha number 40 jodne par mean ka kya hoga. Phir nikaalo.
items.answer: It goes up to 15: total 50 + 40 = 90, and 90 ÷ 6 = 15

items.prompt_en: Kiran says the mean of 2, 4 and 9 must be 4, because the mean is always the middle number. Check.
items.prompt_hi: Kiran kehta hai 2, 4 aur 9 ka mean 4 hi hoga, kyunki mean hamesha beech wala number hota hai. Check karo.
items.answer: Wrong: mean = 15 ÷ 3 = 5; 4 is the median, not the mean
hints: The mean is 5; 4 is the median.

items.prompt_en: Maximum temperatures in a week (°C): 30, 32, 31, 29, 33, 35, 34. What is the mean temperature?

items.prompt_en: A shoe shop wants to know which size to keep the most of. Should it use the mean, median or mode of customers' sizes? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Ek joote ki dukaan jaanna chahti hai ki kaunsa size sabse zyada rakhe. Customers ke size ka mean, median ya mode use kare? Kyun?
items.answer: The mode: it is the size most people buy; a mean like 6.4 is not even a real size

items.prompt_en: Towers of 3, 5, 7 and 9 blocks are levelled so all are equal. How tall is each tower? What is this number called?
items.prompt_hi: 3, 5, 7 aur 9 blocks ke towers ko barabar kar diya. Har tower kitna ooncha hoga? Is number ko kya kehte hain?
items.answer: 6 blocks each; it is the mean (24 ÷ 4)

items.prompt_en: Teach a friend the difference between mean, median and mode, and when to use each.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko mean, median aur mode ka farak sikhao, aur kab kaunsa use karein.
items.answer: Mean: total ÷ count, uses every value but is pulled by extremes; median: middle of the ordered data, good when there are extremes; mode: most frequent, good for things like sizes or favourite choices
hints: Median is the ___ value after ordering; mode is the most frequent.
Mean shares, median is the middle, mode is the most common.

items.prompt_en: From memory: median of 1, 3, 3, 6, 7?

skills.title: Read and compare values on a double bar graph
Choose a sensible scale and plan a double bar graph
Spot misleading graphs: axes not starting at 0, unequal steps, picture sizes

expectations: A double bar graph puts two bars side by side for each category; the legend says which colour is which group
Axis steps must be equal so that equal distances mean equal amounts
If the axis does not start at 0, bar heights exaggerate differences
When a picture is made twice as tall and twice as wide, it looks four times as big
Always read the title, axis labels, scale and legend before believing a graph

misconceptions.belief: Trusts a graph without checking its scale
signs: Judges only by how tall bars look
Does not read the axis numbers
Accepts unequal steps on the axis

diagnostic.prompt_en: A graph's axis is marked 0, 10, 20, 50, 100 with equal gaps between the marks. Is that fair?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek graph ke axis par 0, 10, 20, 50, 100 barabar doori par likhe hain. Kya yeh theek hai?

options.text: No: the steps are not equal (10, 10, 30, 50)

remediation.representation: A ruler with uneven markings beside a fair one
remediation.moveShape: Child measures a bar of 30 on both rulers; ask which ruler tells the truth

misconceptions.belief: Reads bar heights as true comparisons even when the axis does not start at 0
signs: Says B sold twice as much when the bars are 98 and 102 on an axis from 95
Ignores a broken or cut axis
Believes adverts' bar graphs at face value

diagnostic.prompt_en: Shop A sold 98 and Shop B sold 102. On the graph the axis starts at 95, so B's bar looks more than twice as tall. Did B sell twice as much?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Dukaan A ne 98 aur dukaan B ne 102 beche. Graph ka axis 95 se shuru hota hai, isliye B ka bar double se zyada lamba dikhta hai. Kya B ne double becha?

options.text: Yes, the bar is twice as tall

remediation.representation: The same two bars redrawn with the axis from 0
remediation.moveShape: Child redraws the axis starting at 0 and compares; ask how big the difference looks now

misconceptions.belief: Mixes up the two groups in a double bar graph
signs: Reads the boys' bar as the girls'
Ignores the legend
Adds bars of the wrong colour

diagnostic.prompt_en: A double bar graph of favourite games in class 7 (blue = boys, orange = girls): cricket 12 and 7, kho-kho 5 and 9, badminton 7 and 10, football 6 and 3. How many girls chose cricket?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Class 7 ke favourite games ka double bar graph (neela = ladke, naarangi = ladkiyan): cricket 12 aur 7, kho-kho 5 aur 9, badminton 7 aur 10, football 6 aur 3. Kitni ladkiyon ne cricket chuna?

remediation.representation: Legend box enlarged next to the bars with matching colours
remediation.moveShape: Child touches the legend colour first and then the matching bar; ask which colour stands for girls

items.prompt_en: A double bar graph of favourite games in class 7 (blue = boys, orange = girls): cricket 12 and 7, kho-kho 5 and 9, badminton 7 and 10, football 6 and 3. Which game do most girls like?
items.prompt_hi: Class 7 ke favourite games ka double bar graph (neela = ladke, naarangi = ladkiyan): cricket 12 aur 7, kho-kho 5 aur 9, badminton 7 aur 10, football 6 aur 3. Sabse zyada ladkiyon ko kaunsa game pasand hai?
items.answer: Badminton (10 girls)
hints: Look only at the orange bars.

items.prompt_en: A double bar graph of favourite games in class 7 (blue = boys, orange = girls): cricket 12 and 7, kho-kho 5 and 9, badminton 7 and 10, football 6 and 3. How many children in all chose kho-kho?
items.prompt_hi: Class 7 ke favourite games ka double bar graph (neela = ladke, naarangi = ladkiyan): cricket 12 aur 7, kho-kho 5 aur 9, badminton 7 aur 10, football 6 aur 3. Kul kitne bachchon ne kho-kho chuna?
items.answer: 14 (5 boys + 9 girls)

items.prompt_en: A double bar graph of favourite games in class 7 (blue = boys, orange = girls): cricket 12 and 7, kho-kho 5 and 9, badminton 7 and 10, football 6 and 3. For which game is the gap between boys and girls the biggest?
items.prompt_hi: Class 7 ke favourite games ka double bar graph (neela = ladke, naarangi = ladkiyan): cricket 12 aur 7, kho-kho 5 aur 9, badminton 7 aur 10, football 6 aur 3. Kis game mein ladkon aur ladkiyon ke beech sabse bada farak hai?
items.answer: Cricket: 12 − 7 = 5
hints: Find the gap for each game.

items.prompt_en: Two graphs show the same marks, 92 and 96. In graph P the axis starts at 0; in graph Q it starts at 90. Which one makes the difference look big, and which is honest?
items.prompt_hi: Do graph ek hi marks dikhate hain, 92 aur 96. Graph P ka axis 0 se shuru hai; graph Q ka 90 se. Kaunsa farak bada dikhata hai, aur kaunsa imaandaar hai?
items.answer: Q makes 96 look three times 92 (6 vs 2 above 90); P is honest and shows the marks are close
hints: How tall is each bar above 90 in Q?
In P the bars are 92 and 96 tall: ___ the same.

items.prompt_en: An advert's graph shows Brand X at 50% and Brand Y at 48%, with the axis starting at 45%. X's bar looks almost twice as tall. The advert says 'X is far better.' Check.
items.prompt_hi: Ek advert ke graph mein Brand X 50% aur Brand Y 48% hai, axis 45% se shuru hota hai. X ka bar lagbhag double dikhta hai. Advert kehta hai 'X bahut behtar hai.' Check karo.
items.answer: Misleading: the difference is only 2 percentage points; the cut axis makes it look large

items.prompt_en: Your largest value is 240 and your graph has 12 squares of height. What is a good scale, one square = ?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhara sabse bada value 240 hai aur graph mein 12 squares ki height hai. Achha scale kya hoga, ek square = ?
items.answer: 1 square = 20

items.prompt_en: Why must the steps on a graph's axis be equal?
items.prompt_hi: Graph ke axis ke steps barabar kyun hone chahiye?
items.answer: So that equal distances stand for equal amounts; otherwise bar heights mislead
hints: What does the height of a bar show?
If steps are unequal, the same height can mean ___ amounts.
Equal steps make equal distances mean equal amounts.

items.prompt_en: A double bar graph of favourite games in class 7 (blue = boys, orange = girls): cricket 12 and 7, kho-kho 5 and 9, badminton 7 and 10, football 6 and 3. Ankit says 12 girls chose cricket. Check.
items.prompt_hi: Class 7 ke favourite games ka double bar graph (neela = ladke, naarangi = ladkiyan): cricket 12 aur 7, kho-kho 5 aur 9, badminton 7 aur 10, football 6 aur 3. Ankit kehta hai 12 ladkiyon ne cricket chuna. Check karo.
items.answer: Wrong: 12 is the boys' (blue) bar; 7 girls chose cricket

items.prompt_en: Sales were 98 and 102. Predict how the bars look if the axis starts at 95, and if it starts at 0.
items.prompt_hi: Bikri 98 aur 102 thi. Andaaza lagao: axis 95 se shuru ho toh bar kaise dikhenge, aur 0 se shuru ho toh?
items.answer: From 95, the 102 bar looks more than twice as tall (7 vs 3); from 0 the bars look almost equal
hints: How far above 95 is each value?
From 0 the bars are 98 and 102: nearly ___.
Big-looking gap from 95; nearly equal from 0.

items.prompt_en: Plan a double bar graph for rainfall (mm) over three months: Pune 120, 180, 150; Chennai 40, 60, 110. What goes on each axis, what scale, and what does the legend show?
items.prompt_hi: Teen mahine ki baarish (mm) ke liye double bar graph plan karo: Pune 120, 180, 150; Chennai 40, 60, 110. Kaunse axis par kya, scale kya, aur legend kya dikhayega?
items.answer: Months on the horizontal axis, rainfall in mm on the vertical axis from 0 in equal steps (e.g. 20 mm), two bars per month, legend: one colour Pune, one colour Chennai
hints: The largest value is 180, so steps of ___ mm work.
Months across, mm up from 0, two colours in the legend.

items.prompt_en: A magazine shows that phone sales doubled, using a phone picture made twice as tall AND twice as wide. Why is this misleading?
items.prompt_hi: Ek magazine dikhati hai ki phone ki bikri double hui, phone ki tasveer ko double lamba AUR double chauda karke. Yeh misleading kyun hai?
items.answer: Twice as tall and twice as wide covers 4 times the area, so it looks like 4 times the sales, not 2
hints: What happens to area when both sides double?
The picture covers ___ times the space.
It looks 4 times bigger, though sales only doubled.

items.prompt_en: Teach a friend a checklist for deciding whether to trust a graph.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko ek checklist sikhao ki kisi graph par bharosa karein ya nahi.
items.answer: Read the title and labels, check the axis starts at 0 and has equal steps, read the legend, and compare the actual numbers rather than the look
hints: Then check the axis: starts at ___ and equal steps.
Labels, axis from 0, equal steps, legend, real numbers.

items.prompt_en: From memory: in a double bar graph, what tells you which bar belongs to which group?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se: double bar graph mein kaun batata hai ki kaunsa bar kis group ka hai?
items.answer: The legend (key)
hints: It is usually in a box at the corner.

items.prompt_hi: Kya y = 4, 2y + 7 = 16 ka hal hai?
items.answer: No: 2 × 4 + 7 = 15, not 16 (the solution is 4.5)

items.prompt_en: Find the mistake: 3x + 5 = 20 → 3x = 25 → x = 25/3.
items.prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo: 3x + 5 = 20 → 3x = 25 → x = 25/3.
items.answer: Line 2: 5 should be subtracted, not added; 3x = 15, so x = 5

items.prompt_en: Find the mistake: 2(x + 4) = 18 → 2x + 4 = 18 → 2x = 14 → x = 7.
items.answer: Line 2: the 4 must also be doubled; 2x + 8 = 18, 2x = 10, x = 5

items.prompt_en: Find the mistake: x ÷ 3 = 6 → x = 2.
items.prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo: x ÷ 3 = 6 → x = 2.
items.answer: Wrong operation: undo ÷ 3 by multiplying by 3, so x = 18

items.prompt_en: Find the mistake: 5 − x = 2 → x = 2 − 5 = −3.
items.prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo: 5 − x = 2 → x = 2 − 5 = −3.
items.answer: x = 3: check 5 − (−3) = 8, not 2; add x to both sides, 5 = 2 + x, so x = 3
hints: Add x to both sides: 5 = 2 + x, so x = ___.

items.prompt_en: Why should you check your answer in the original equation, not in a later line?
items.prompt_hi: Apna answer original equation mein check kyun karna chahiye, baad wali line mein kyun nahi?
items.answer: A later line may already contain the mistake, so the answer can fit it but not the real problem
acceptable: the later line may be wrong
hints: In any line after the first.
Checking after the mistake will ___ catch it.
Only the original equation is sure to be right.

items.prompt_en: A neat solution of 3x + 2 = 17 ends with x = 4. Predict whether it is right before checking, then check.
items.prompt_hi: 3x + 2 = 17 ka saaf hal x = 4 par khatam hota hai. Check se pehle andaaza lagao ki sahi hai ya nahi, phir check karo.
items.answer: Wrong: 3 × 4 + 2 = 14, not 17; the right answer is x = 5

items.prompt_en: Two solutions of 4x = 2x + 10. A: 4x − 2x = 10, 2x = 10, x = 5. B: 4x + 2x = 10, 6x = 10, x = 10/6. Which is right, and what did B do wrong?
items.prompt_hi: 4x = 2x + 10 ke do hal. A: 4x − 2x = 10, 2x = 10, x = 5. B: 4x + 2x = 10, 6x = 10, x = 10/6. Kaunsa sahi hai, aur B ne kya galti ki?
items.answer: A is right (x = 5); B moved 2x without changing + to −, i.e. did not subtract 2x from both sides
hints: B should have ___ 2x from both sides.
A; B forgot to change the sign.

items.prompt_en: A friend solved '3 pens and a ₹15 notebook cost ₹60' as 3p + 15 = 60 → 3p = 75 → p = 25. Find the mistake and the real price of a pen.
items.prompt_hi: Ek dost ne '3 pen aur ₹15 ki copy ₹60 ke' ko aise hal kiya: 3p + 15 = 60 → 3p = 75 → p = 25. Galti dhoondo aur pen ka asli daam batao.
items.answer: ₹15 per pen: the 15 should be subtracted (3p = 45), not added
hints: Check: do 3 pens at ₹25 plus ₹15 make ₹60?

items.prompt_en: Use a balance to show why 'x + 7 = 12 → x = 12 + 7' is wrong.
items.prompt_hi: Taraazu se dikhao ki 'x + 7 = 12 → x = 12 + 7' galat kyun hai.
items.answer: Taking 7 off the left pan means taking 7 off the right pan too, so x = 12 − 7 = 5
hints: What do you remove from the left pan?

items.prompt_en: Teach a friend how to hunt for a bug in someone's solution.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao ki kisi ke hal mein galti kaise dhoondhein.
items.answer: Put the answer into the original equation; if it fails, check that each line follows from the one before by the same operation on both sides; fix the first wrong line and check again
hints: What is the quickest first test?
Substitute the answer in the original.
Then check each line follows from the ___ one.
Test, find the first wrong line, fix, re-test.

items.prompt_en: Asha solved 2x + 1 = 11 like this: 2x = 11 − 1 = 10, then x = 10 − 5 = 5. Her answer is right. Is her working right?
items.prompt_hi: Asha ne 2x + 1 = 11 aise hal kiya: 2x = 11 − 1 = 10, phir x = 10 − 5 = 5. Answer sahi hai. Kya working sahi hai?
items.answer: No: from 2x = 10 you divide by 2; subtracting 5 only happened to give 5 (it fails for 2x = 12)
hints: Try her method on 2x = 12: 12 − 5 = ___, but x should be 6.
